cost_note: cost_usd = typical managed-service monthly cost per data/scale tier (<1k, 1k-10k, 10k-100k, 100k-1M, 1M-10M, >10M DAU). Self-hosting can be cheaper but adds ops work. entry_plans = vendor free and small fixed-price plans, each with the largest scale tier (0 = <1k DAU) and data size (GB within 12 months) it holds; the cheapest plan that holds the project sets the floor, and a $0 floor with no plan that holds the project becomes the next tier's floor. Each plan names its vendor; the cost estimate uses a plan only when the stack's managed offering on its host is that vendor's, and under HIPAA only a plan marked baa (the vendor signs a Business Associate Agreement for it). host_plans = the smallest plan of a host's own managed database, used only by the cost estimate on that host.
model_note: models = fit (1-5) for each data shape (search = full-text or log search is the main way the data is read). consistency = strongest guarantee available for multi-record transactions.

Sorted sets for leaderboards/matchmaking
weaknesses: Memory-bound and asynchronously replicated: not a system of record for money or health data

system_of_record.why: In-memory store: with the default append-only-file setting (fsync every second) a crash loses up to the last second of writes, and snapshots alone lose minutes; it holds key-value data but not tables of records

items.name: ClickHouse
items.summary: Columnar OLAP database for real-time analytics over billions of rows.
strengths: Aggregations over billions of rows in sub-second time
High compression for event/log/telemetry data
weaknesses: Not for transactional row updates or point lookups with strict consistency

items.name: OpenSearch / Elasticsearch
items.summary: Distributed search engine on Lucene inverted indexes: full-text search with relevance ranking, log search and aggregations over JSON documents.

managed_offerings.azure: Elastic Cloud on Azure (Azure Native ISV Service)

strengths: Full-text search with relevance ranking, highlighting, facets and typo tolerance
Log and event search over terabytes with index lifecycle policies (hot, warm, delete)
weaknesses: Not a transactional store: no multi-document transactions, and new writes become searchable after a refresh (about 1 s)
Cluster sizing (shards, replicas, JVM heap) and upgrades take real operations work

system_of_record.why: Search index: no multi-document transactions, and a write becomes searchable only after the next refresh, so it keeps append-only events (logs) but records that are updated belong in a transactional store it indexes from

items.name: Neo4j
items.summary: Native graph database queried with Cypher; built for relationship-heavy traversals.
strengths: Multi-hop traversals (friends-of-friends, fraud rings, recommendations) in milliseconds
Graph data science library
weaknesses: Write scale-out is limited compared with distributed stores
Usually a secondary store alongside a relational system of record

system_of_record.why: Graph store: built for relationship traversals, and fits tables of records 2/5; graph deployments typically sit beside the relational system of record (Neo4j's own financial-services case kept SQL Server for customer history and added the graph for link analysis)

items.name: Cloud Firestore
items.summary: Google's serverless document database with realtime listeners and offline client caching.
strengths: Realtime listeners + offline persistence out of the box
Zero ops; scales automatically
weaknesses: Limited querying (no joins, restricted aggregations)
Per-document read billing; Google advises against high write rates to a single document (the sustainable rate depends on the workload), so hot counters need sharding

Write rate grows only gradually: Google's 500/50/5 rule starts new traffic at 500 operations a second and adds 50% every 5 minutes, and an indexed field with sequential values (such as a message timestamp) caps a collection at 500 writes a second
Google Cloud lock-in

usage.note: Firestore bills per document read and write (free quota of 50,000 reads and 20,000 writes a day) plus stored GB.
